questions.question: Which blood vessels carry blood back towards the heart?
questions.options: nerves | veins | windpipes | arteries
questions.explanation: Veins bring blood back to the heart. Arteries carry it away, and nerves carry messages, not blood.
questions.sourceUnitTitle: Humans and Animals: Your Amazing Body Systems

questions.question: Amina runs a fast race. Why does she breathe more deeply afterwards?
questions.options: Her stomach needs air to digest food | Her lungs have grown bigger during the race | Her muscles need more oxygen and must get rid of more carbon dioxide | Her blood has stopped moving
questions.correctAnswer: Her muscles need more oxygen and must get rid of more carbon dioxide
questions.explanation: Hard work uses up oxygen quickly and makes extra carbon dioxide, so the lungs work harder to swap them.
questions.sourceUnitTitle: Humans and Animals: Your Amazing Body Systems

questions.question: What is the main job of the digestive system?
questions.options: To pump blood around the body | To keep the body cool in hot weather | To carry messages to the muscles | To break food down into nutrients the body can use
questions.correctAnswer: To break food down into nutrients the body can use
questions.explanation: Digestion turns the food you eat into small nutrients that the blood can carry to every part of you.
questions.sourceUnitTitle: Humans and Animals: Your Amazing Body Systems

questions.question: Yusuf counts 18 beats of his pulse in 15 seconds. What is his heart rate in beats per minute?
questions.explanation: There are four lots of 15 seconds in a minute, so 18 × 4 = 72 beats per minute.
questions.sourceUnitTitle: Humans and Animals: Your Amazing Body Systems

questions.question: A group of organs that work together to do one big job is called a:
questions.options: nutrient | organ system | skeleton | habitat
questions.explanation: The heart and blood vessels together make the circulatory system — organs teaming up form an organ system.
questions.sourceUnitTitle: Humans and Animals: Your Amazing Body Systems

questions.question: In the food chain grass → goat → lion, what is the goat?
questions.options: a solvent | a consumer | a decomposer | a producer
questions.explanation: The goat eats another living thing instead of making its own food, so it is a consumer.

questions.question: What does every food chain start with?
questions.options: a meat-eating animal | a fungus | a rock | a producer such as a plant
questions.correctAnswer: a producer such as a plant
questions.explanation: Plants use sunlight to make their own food, so they are the producers every food chain begins with.

questions.question: Fungi and bacteria break down dead leaves and return nutrients to the soil. What are living things like these called?
questions.options: predators | producers | herbivores | decomposers
questions.explanation: Decomposers are nature’s recyclers: they break down dead material so the nutrients can be used again.

questions.question: Why does a scientist often draw a food web instead of a single food chain?
questions.options: Because a food web shows the weather | Because a food web is quicker to draw | Because food chains are always wrong | Because most animals eat more than one kind of food, so many chains link together
questions.correctAnswer: Because most animals eat more than one kind of food, so many chains link together
questions.explanation: A web shows the real tangle of who eats whom, which one straight chain cannot show.

questions.question: A village cuts down all the trees along a riverbank. What is the most likely result?
questions.options: The soil becomes much richer | Soil is washed away and animals lose their homes | The river water becomes cleaner | More rain falls the next day
questions.correctAnswer: Soil is washed away and animals lose their homes
questions.explanation: Tree roots hold the soil in place and their branches are homes, so removing them harms the habitat.

questions.question: Which change makes a brand new material and cannot easily be undone?
questions.options: melting ice | boiling water | burning wood | dissolving sugar in tea
questions.explanation: Burning makes ash and smoke, which are new materials. The other three only change the state or mix things together.

questions.question: Muna stirs sugar into a cup of water until it disappears. In this solution, what is the sugar called?
questions.options: the residue | the solvent | the filter | the solute
questions.explanation: The solute is the material that dissolves; the liquid doing the dissolving, the water, is the solvent.

questions.question: You want to get the salt back out of a cup of salty water. Which method should you choose?
questions.options: hold a magnet over it | let the water evaporate | pour it through filter paper | add more water
questions.explanation: The dissolved salt is left behind when the water evaporates away. A filter cannot catch something that is dissolved.

questions.question: Salty, muddy water is poured through filter paper. The mud is caught but the water still tastes salty. Why?
questions.options: The salt has turned into water | Filter paper always removes salt first | The mud took the salt with it | The salt is dissolved, so it passes through with the water
questions.correctAnswer: The salt is dissolved, so it passes through with the water
questions.explanation: Dissolved salt is spread out between the water particles, far too small for filter paper to hold back.

questions.question: Which force slows down a ball as it rolls across a rough mat?
questions.options: magnetism | friction | gravity | electricity
questions.explanation: Friction acts between two surfaces that rub together and always pushes against the movement.

questions.question: A box has a mass of 6 kg. On Earth gravity pulls with about 10 N for each kilogram. What is the weight of the box?
questions.explanation: Weight = mass × gravity, so 6 × 10 = 60 N. Mass is measured in kilograms and weight is a force measured in newtons.

questions.question: A paper parachute makes a small toy fall slowly to the ground. Which force is slowing the toy down?
questions.options: air resistance | magnetism | gravity | upthrust from the floor
questions.explanation: The wide parachute pushes against lots of air, and that air resistance works against the pull of gravity.

questions.question: A book rests on a table and does not move. What can you say about the forces acting on it?
questions.options: They are unbalanced | They are balanced | There are no forces on the book | Gravity has stopped working
questions.explanation: Gravity pulls the book down and the table pushes it up by the same amount, so the forces balance and nothing moves.

questions.question: Why is an electrical wire made of copper but covered in plastic?
questions.options: Copper is cheaper than plastic | Both materials conduct equally well | Copper conducts the electricity and the plastic insulates to keep us safe | Plastic carries the electricity and copper stops it
questions.correctAnswer: Copper conducts the electricity and the plastic insulates to keep us safe
questions.explanation: Metals like copper let current flow easily, while plastic is an insulator that keeps the current inside the wire.

questions.question: Faisal builds a circuit but his bulb will not light, even though the cell and bulb are both new and working. What should he check first?
questions.options: whether the room is warm enough | whether the bulb is the right colour | whether there is a gap so the loop is not complete | whether the wires are long enough to reach the floor
questions.correctAnswer: whether there is a gap so the loop is not complete
questions.explanation: Current can only flow around a complete loop, so a loose wire or an open switch is the usual reason a good bulb stays dark.

questions.question: Which object placed in a gap in the wire would let the circuit keep working?
questions.options: a rubber band | a dry wooden stick | a plastic ruler | a steel nail
questions.explanation: Steel is a metal, and metals are conductors, so the current can travel straight through the nail.

questions.question: What does a switch do in a circuit?
questions.options: It opens or closes the loop to stop or start the current | It measures force in newtons | It changes the colour of the wire | It stores electricity for later
questions.correctAnswer: It opens or closes the loop to stop or start the current
questions.explanation: Closing a switch completes the loop so current flows; opening it makes a gap and everything switches off.

questions.question: What does a seed need before it can germinate?
questions.options: only bright sunlight | salt, sugar and sand | water, warmth and air | only cold and darkness
questions.explanation: A resting seed wakes up when it has water, warmth and air. It uses its own food store until the first leaves appear.

questions.question: Which part of a flower catches the pollen when a bee brushes past?
questions.options: the petal | the anther | the stigma | the root
questions.explanation: The sticky stigma is the top of the female part of the flower, ready to catch pollen for pollination.

questions.question: Washing on a line dries faster on a hot, windy day. Why?
questions.options: Heat and moving air make the water evaporate faster | The washing gets heavier as it dries | Water freezes in the sunshine | The clothes soak up the wind
questions.correctAnswer: Heat and moving air make the water evaporate faster
questions.explanation: Evaporation speeds up when it is warm and windy, so the water leaves the cloth as invisible water vapour more quickly.

questions.question: Which sentence describes the particles in a gas?
questions.options: joined together in one solid block | far apart and moving quickly in all directions | packed closely but able to slide past each other | locked tightly in fixed places
questions.correctAnswer: far apart and moving quickly in all directions
questions.explanation: Gas particles are spread out and fast-moving, which is why a gas fills whatever container you put it in.

questions.question: You can see a wooden chair in a bright room. Why?
questions.options: The chair is transparent | Light bounces off the chair and travels into your eyes | Your eyes send out light beams to touch the chair | The chair makes its own light
questions.correctAnswer: Light bounces off the chair and travels into your eyes
questions.explanation: Objects that do not make light are seen because they reflect light from a source into our eyes.

questions.question: Halima holds a toy between a torch and the wall, then moves the toy further away from the torch. Its shadow becomes:
questions.options: many colours | brighter than the wall | smaller | larger
questions.explanation: The further the object is from the light, the less of the light it blocks, so the shadow shrinks.

questions.question: Why do we have day and night?
questions.options: The Sun switches off at night | The Earth spins once on its axis every 24 hours | The Moon covers the Sun each evening | The Earth travels around the Sun once a day
questions.correctAnswer: The Earth spins once on its axis every 24 hours
questions.explanation: As the Earth turns, your side faces the Sun for daytime and then turns away into night.

questions.question: How long does the Earth take to travel once all the way around the Sun?
questions.options: about 12 hours | about 24 hours | about 365 days | about 29.5 days
questions.explanation: One full orbit of the Sun is one year, which is about 365 days.

questions.question: Which of these shows that something is a living thing?
questions.options: It grows and can make new living things | It is hard and shiny | It can be pushed along by the wind | It floats on water
questions.correctAnswer: It grows and can make new living things
questions.explanation: Living things grow, feed and reproduce. Being shiny or moving in the wind does not make something alive.

questions.question: Which object would a magnet pull towards itself?
questions.options: an iron nail | a wooden stick | a glass marble | a plastic spoon
questions.explanation: Magnets attract magnetic metals such as iron and steel, but not plastic, glass or wood.

questions.question: A material you can see through clearly, like clean window glass, is:
questions.options: magnetic | transparent | opaque | translucent
questions.explanation: Transparent materials let nearly all the light straight through, so you can see clearly through them.

questions.question: Water vapour touches a cold window and turns back into drops of water. This change is called:
questions.options: evaporation | condensation | dissolving | melting
questions.explanation: Condensation happens when a gas cools down and becomes a liquid again.

questions.question: Which layer of the Earth do we live on?
questions.options: the mantle | the outer core | the inner core | the crust
questions.explanation: The crust is the thin, solid outer layer of the Earth, with the much hotter mantle and core underneath.

questions.question: For a bulb to light up, the circuit must:
questions.options: have a gap in the wire | be soaking wet | be built only from plastic parts | make a complete loop from the cell and back again
questions.correctAnswer: make a complete loop from the cell and back again
questions.explanation: Electricity can only flow all the way round a closed loop, so any gap stops the bulb lighting.
